## Introduction

- What is Linked Art?
- Why manuscripts need special treatment?

::: notes
Presenter:
Welcome everyone! Today we’ll dive into how Linked Art models manuscripts. We’ll cover the difference between the *Work* (the conceptual text) and the *Object* (the physical codex or scroll), and see concrete JSON-LD examples.
:::

---

## Core JSON-LD Structure

Every Linked Art document needs:

- `@context` – Linked Art JSON-LD context URI  
- `id` – Unique HTTP(S) URI  
- `type` – CIDOC-CRM class or RDF class . (e.g., `HumanMadeObject`, `LinguisticObject`, `Actor`, `Event`)  
- `_label` – Human-readable label  

::: notes
Presenter:
Quick refresher on the fundamentals: context, URI identity, RDF type, and the display label. This baseline applies to manuscripts just as much as paintings or digital items.
:::

---

## Core Classes for Manuscripts

| Class               | Role                                 |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------|
| **LinguisticObject**| The *text* content (Work)            |
| **HumanMadeObject** | The *physical* codex or scroll (Object) |
| **DigitalObject**   | Scanned or born-digital images/text  |
| **Dimension**       | Measurements (leaves, folios, size)  |
| **Type**            | Material categories (parchment, paper) |

Reference: [LinkedArt, Basic Patterns](https://linked.art/model/base/)


::: notes
Presenter:
Here are the key classes. Note that the *Work* side is covered by `LinguisticObject`, while the *Object* side is `HumanMadeObject`. We’ll dive deeper next.
:::

---

## Manuscript Work vs. Manuscript Object

| Aspect                 | Manuscript **Work**                     | Manuscript **Object**                       |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| **Definition**         | The intellectual text (author, title)   | The physical codex or scroll                 |
| **Type**               | `Work` (a subclass of PropositionalObject) | `HumanMadeObject`                            |
| **Key Properties**     | `title`, `creator`, `language`, `subject` | `material`, `carrier`, `dimensions`, `binding` |
| **Relationships**      | `derived_from`, `translation_of`        | `material_used`, `physical_production`       |


::: notes
Presenter:
Emphasize: the *Work* is conceptual; the *Object* is tangible. A single Work may have multiple Objects (e.g., two copies), and one Object carries exactly one Work.
:::

---

## JSON-LD Example: Work

```yaml
id: "https://data.example.org/work/001"
type: Work
_label: "Codex Gigas"
title: "Codex Gigas"
creator:
  - type: Person
    _label: "Brother Herman"
language: 
  - _label: "Latin"
subject:
  - _label: "Religious texts"
derived_from: []
```

::: notes 
Presenter
This slide shows how you’d declare the Work. You see type: Work, the _label and properties like creator and language.
:::

---

## JSON-LD Example: Object

```yaml
id: "https://data.example.org/object/001a"
type: HumanMadeObject
_label: "Codex Gigas (Prague Copy)"
carries:
  - type: LinguisticObject
    id: "https://data.example.org/work/001"
    _label: "Codex Gigas"
material:
  - _label: "Parchment"
dimension:
  - type: Dimension
    value: 636
    _label: "Leaves"
binding:
  - _label: "Wooden boards with leather"
currentOwner:
  - type: Group
    _label: "Prague National Library"
```

::: notes 
Presenter:
Here’s the Object. Notice carries linking back to the Work, and the physical attributes (material, dimension, binding, currentOwner). 
:::

---

## Which Properties Belong Where?

- Work

    - Intellectual properties: `title`, `language`, `subject`, `derived_from`, `translation_of`

- Object

    - Physical properties: `material`, `dimension`, `binding`, `production`, `currentOwner`

::: notes 
Presenter:
Summarize: don’t mix up text-centric and object-centric properties. If you’re describing the content: it’s a Work. If you’re describing the codex: it’s an Object. 
:::


---

## Structural Link: carries

The Object carries the Work:

```yaml
carries:
  - type: LinguisticObject
    id: <Work URI>
    _label: <Work label>
```
- Ensures clear separation and linkage.

::: notes 
Presenter:
Remember: carries is the magic property that connects the physical container to the conceptual text. Always include it for manuscripts. 
:::

---

## Recap & Best Practices

- Model the intellectual text as Work (type: Work or LinguisticObject subclass).

- Model the physical codex as Object (type: HumanMadeObject).

- Link via carries.

- Keep physical vs. conceptual properties distinct.

- Use controlled vocabularies for materials, dimensions, binding types.


::: notes 
Presenter:
Wrap up with these five take-aways. They’ll guide you whether you’re modeling a medieval codex or a modern artist’s book in Linked Art. 
:::

---

## Overview of the JSON-LD

- We’ll unpack each part of this JSON-LD document:
  
  1. Top-Level Identity  
  2. Work linkage (`carries`)  
  3. Collection membership (`member_of`)  
  4. Equivalencies (`equivalent`)  
  5. Related texts (`subject_of`)  
  6. Classification (`classified_as`)  
  7. Identifiers & Names (`identified_by`)  
  8. Descriptive statements (`referred_to_by`)  
  9. Thumbnail representation (`representation`)  
  10. API links (`_links`)


::: notes
Presenter:
This slide lays out our roadmap. We’ve got a complex object; let’s break it into digestible pieces.
:::


---

## Top-Level Identity

```json
{
  "id": "https://lux.collections.yale.edu/data/object/709fe0da-ac43-40ed-9a46-2b099460c655",
  "type": "HumanMadeObject",
  "_label": "Diary of Alfred Gurton on a trip to India",
  "carries": [
    {
      "id": "https://lux.collections.yale.edu/data/text/ffb63bd1-7ed8-4de2-9292-defb374b53f0",
      "type": "LinguisticObject",
      "_label": "Diary of Alfred Gurton on a trip to India"
    }
  ],
  "@context": "https://linked.art/ns/v1/linked-art.json"}
```

- `id`: Unique HTTP URI

- `type`: CIDOC-CRM class → physical object

- `_label:` Human-readable title

- `@context:` Linked Art JSON-LD context


::: notes 
Presenter:
Every Linked Art document begins with these. They ground the object in CIDOC-CRM and JSON-LD.
:::


---

## Linking to the Work (carries)

```json
  "carries": [
    {
      "id": "https://lux.collections.yale.edu/data/text/ffb63bd1-7ed8-4de2-9292-defb374b53f0",
      "type": "LinguisticObject",
      "_label": "Diary of Alfred Gurton on a trip to India"
    }
  ]
```

The Object “carries” the Work (the text)

- type: `LinguisticObject` marks the conceptual diary content

::: notes
Presenter:
This crucial link separates the physical codex (Object) from its text (Work). 
:::

---

## Collection Membership (member_of)

```json
  "member_of": [
    {
      "id": "https://lux.collections.yale.edu/data/set/6d003cce-882b-45e2-896d-6462d7f0114c",
      "type": "Set",
      "_label": "Rare Books and Manuscripts, Yale Center for British Art"
    }
  ]
```

- Indicates this object’s belonging to a named collection or set

::: notes 
Presenter:
Use member_of when you need to show collection structure in Linked Art. 
:::


---

## Equivalencies (equivalent)

```json
"equivalent": [
  {
    "id": "https://linked-art.library.yale.edu/node/ce5f592d-c116-454a-9f2a-881e0b82fbb7",
    "type": "HumanMadeObject",
    "_label": "Diary of Alfred Gurton on a trip to India"
  }
]
```

- Points to alternate URIs for the same object

- Supports interoperability across systems

::: notes 
Presenter:
Whenever your object appears under multiple domains or APIs, use equivalent. 
:::

## Hypermedia Links (_links)

```json
{
  "_links": {
    "curies": [
      {
        "name": "la",
        "href": "https://linked.art/api/1.0/rels/{rel}",
        "templated": true
      },
      {
        "name": "lux",
        "href": "https://lux.collections.yale.edu/api/rels/{rel}",
        "templated": true
      }
    ],
    "self": {
      "href": "https://lux.collections.yale.edu/data/object/709fe0da-ac43-40ed-9a46-2b099460c655"
    },
    "lux:itemDepartment": {
      "href": "https://lux.collections.yale.edu/api/search/agent?q=%7B%22curated%22%3A%7B%22containingItem%22%3A%7B%22id%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Flux.collections.yale.edu%2Fdata%2Fobject%2F709fe0da-ac43-40ed-9a46-2b099460c655%22%7D%7D%7D",
      "_estimate": 1
    },
    "lux:itemUnit": {
      "href": "https://lux.collections.yale.edu/api/facets/item?q=%7B%22id%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Flux.collections.yale.edu%2Fdata%2Fobject%2F709fe0da-ac43-40ed-9a46-2b099460c655%22%7D&name=responsibleUnits",
      "_estimate": 1
    }
  }
}

```

- Curies for link-rel namespaces

- `self` for the canonical URI

- Custom API controls (`lux:` prefixes)


::: notes 
Presenter:
Finally, _links provide navigational affordances for clients and browsers. 
:::

---

##  Recap

- **Object vs. Work** - `HumanMadeObject` + `carries:LinguisticObject`

- Membership, equivalencies, and hypermedia via `member_of`/`equivalent`/`_links`

- Textual and digital relationships via `subject_of`

- Tagging & identification via `classified_as`/`identified_by`

- Free text with `referred_to_by` and visuals with `representation`


::: notes 
Presenter:
Keep this template handy—most Linked Art objects follow the same pattern, with domain-specific tweaks for manuscripts. 
:::

## Context & Namespaces

- Item: [Horace Walpole's Journal, 1783-1791](https://lux.collections.yale.edu/view/object/0482665f-bd9f-47fc-a86f-e78e66c5e00b)

- [Record in Quicksearch](https://search.library.yale.edu/catalog/14962535)

```json
 "@context": "https://linked.art/ns/v1/linked-art.json"
```

- Declares term definitions (classes & properties).
- Ensures consistent interpretation by clients.

## Top-Level Identity

- Item: Horace Walpole's Journal, 1783-1791

```json
{
  "id": "https://lux.collections.yale.edu/data/object/0482665f-bd9f-47fc-a86f-e78e66c5e00b",
  "type": "HumanMadeObject",
  "_label": "Horace Walpole's Journal, 1783-1791",
}
```

- **id**: Unique URI for the object.
- **type**: Linked Art class of the object.
- **_label**: Human-readable title.

- Item: Horace Walpole's Journal, 1783-1791

```json
      "type": "LinguisticObject",

    }
  ]
```

- Links the physical object to its textual content.
